distributions._main_world_doc: G87. WHERE A TRAVELLER MAIN WORLD GOES AND WHAT IT IS, as data a GM can tweak without a release. Read by worlds/mainWorldPlacement.ts. The engine used to decide this from a table of Sol's orbital spacing indexed by the star's spectral LETTER, so every G star put its main world at 0.85 AU and every M star at 0.17 AU whatever their real luminosity. It now asks physics/zones.ts where THAT star's habitable zone is and places the world inside it. THE PROFILES BELOW ARE MATCHED IN ORDER OF TOLERANCE, best first: the engine takes the most comfortable grade the UWP's own atmosphere and hydrographics can honestly support, and works DOWN rather than giving up - the owner's rule is that somebody is placed unless nobody could live there at all, even if they live underground. `template` is a GENERATION template and must be a real statTemplates key. `readsAs` is what the classifier is EXPECTED to call the finished world; it is DERIVED from the world's physics and must never be fed back in as an input.
distributions._main_world_bypass_doc: G87. TRAVELLER'S OWN DATA IS THE AUTHORITY, and a world its codes declare hostile is never quietly moved somewhere kinder - which is the user's own bypass request and the steer-don't-stop rule agreeing with each other. A world carrying any of these keeps exactly the orbit today's code gives it. Keyed on the codes traveller/decoder.ts already expands, so a GM can add one without a release.

surface_albedo._note: Bond-albedo surface model (inbox B5, B68). Bare ground from the makeup, then brightened by the deposits the engine already derives: wind-laid oxide dust, and any surface volatile frozen out of the atmosphere. A FROZEN SOLVENT SHELL is different from either and ages: `ice_clean` is a fresh slab, `ice_lag` is the dark non-ice residue that builds on it, and `ice_lag_half_age_Gyr` is the surface age at which the lag covers half of it. `frost` is a coating condensing out of the air NOW (calibrated on Io) and does not age - two states of one material.
